messages.author: b80a86909a46ffa5
messages.subject: h1.information "unstructured" or "structured"?
parts:
hello,

I'm running a model with the MLMV estimator, and found that CFI and TLI don't get "Robust" values; that is: there are values for CFI and TLI in the "Robust" column, but not for the two additional output rows labeled "Robust Comparative Fit Index" and "Robust Tucker-Lewis Index.

I found this related issue: https://github.com/yrosseel/lavaan/issues/95

The suggested solution is to pass the argument h1.information="unstructured", however, this does not solve the missing Robust values of CFI and TLI. But,  I found that the CFI/TLI values in the robust column do get better (> .97, >.96 ) when passing h1.information="unstructured" and this by itself is useful in order to secure good fit values. So my question is really about the h1.information argument.

There is very little information about what this argument does beyond a short description. What does it mean to pass "unstructured" for the h1.information argument and is it warranted in this case to use it? What is the drawback of passing "unstructured", instead of the default "structured"?  I'd prefer to know what I'm tweaking here.

klaas

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: h1.information "unstructured" or "structured"?
parts: I'm running a model with the MLMV estimator, and found that CFI and TLI don't get "Robust" values

I expect because they were not originally defined for mean- AND variance-adjusted statistics, only for mean-adjusted statistics.  Recently they were adapted for MLMV (but not recommended for WLSMV).  See details here:  https://doi.org/10.1080/00273171.2018.1455142
I found this related issue: https://github.com/yrosseel/lavaan/issues/95

I don't think this is related.  That issue was about someone using MLM, not MLMV.  The V is the issue, and I don't think that has been incorporated into lavaan yet.  I might be wrong.
 
Terrence D. Jorgensen
Assistant Professor, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
http://www.uva.nl/profile/t.d.jorgensen

messages.author: b80a86909a46ffa5
messages.subject: Re: h1.information "unstructured" or "structured"?
parts:
Thanks Terrence for clarifying that and the link to the relevant literature.

As for the issue of using h1.information="structured" vs. ="unstructured":  Yves explained in a comment on that GitHub issue the difference:

"Structured means that the 'sigma' in the formula is replaced by the model-implied sigma. Unstructured means that 'sigma' is replaced by the sample-based covariance matrix."

It seems (from googling on this topic) that the default is "structured" (and that "unstructured" is only used when using DWLS estimator); but I can't find any information about the rationale for this option, or the trade-offs involved in setting it to either "structured" or "unstructured". My model fit gets better with h1.information="unstructured". Is there any theoretical/methodological justification for using "unstructured"? None of the books on SEM seems to discuss this option.

klaas
